geom_node_col: Bar plot at each node
description:
The `geom_node_tile()` draws nodes as tiles with center provided by the layout's `x` and `y` components and with `width` and `height` from the `geom_node_tile()`'s mapping. That's very useful.

I have a slightly different use-case: I wish to be able to draw something like a `geom_col()` at each node. I.e. two (or more) bars and not just a tile. The problem with `geom_node_tile()` is that as with `geom_tile()`, the `x` and `y` give the center, so comparing two bars/tiles is difficult as positioning from the center is fundamentally wrong.

I am wondering what you think would be the best way solving this? I have a few suggestions myself:

1) Try to solve it in generality by making it possible for nodes to each have a `geom_col()`.
2) Implement `geom_node_rect()` using `geom_rect()` with it's `xmin`, `xmax`, `ymin` and `ymax` parameters. I am not sure if sensible default values can be provided. 
3) Make extra arguments to `geom_node_tile()`: `hjust` and `vjust`: The default `hjust = 0.5` and `vjust = 0.5` gives functionality as now. In my case I would do something like `hjust = 0` and `hjust = 0.5`. Here, the problem is that the bars will use the same y coordinate.

Do you have any input on this?

I would prefer solving it in generality by a `geom_node_col()` as suggested in 1), but I'm not sure if that's possible.

title: Feature request: double-headed (bidirectional) arrows
description:
For some applications, it is useful to have bidirectional arrows. Maybe the `arrow` argument can turn into an `arrow_end` and `arrow_start` argument?

I'm trying to create simple graph visualisations of structural equation models from a fitted `lavaan` object like so:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11596858/78164897-cd5c4680-744a-11ea-804e-2ebeea8c98a5.png)


`ggraph` seems like a really good choice for this! It's already looking quite good with the "tree" layout and the parameter estimates for this model in there!

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11596858/78165283-612e1280-744b-11ea-8dec-2ef85fce4388.png)

I intend to make layout functions for the most common types of models. The only missing part (to my knowledge) is double-headed arrows.

title: trying to fill each circle with a manually specified color of vertex attribute
description:
I am trying to represent a graph as a circle packing plot using R / igraph / ggraph:
```
    df <- read.table("elist.txt", header=F, sep="\t")
    df2 <- read.table("vlist.txt", header=F, sep="\t")
    mygraph <- graph_from_data_frame(df, vertices=df2)
    ggraph(mygraph, layout = 'circlepack') + geom_node_circle() +
      geom_node_text(aes(label=as.character(name))) + coord_fixed()


```
This works. But I want each node to be filled in a color which I specified as a vertex attribute of `mygraph`. So I am trying to do s/th like:
```
geom_node_circle(aes(fill=V2))
```
With incomprehensible results.

How can I solve this? I am trying to fill each circle with a manually specified color, where color is either a name as a string (or even better would be a hex code).

[elist.txt](https://github.com/thomasp85/ggraph/files/4346288/elist.txt)
[vlist.txt](https://github.com/thomasp85/ggraph/files/4346289/vlist.txt)

title: Is it possible to apply a condition to show.legend?
description:
My idea is to show only one legend that belongs to a selected year among many lists of network graphs. 
I added a condition to `show.legend` and got a somewhat surprising result.
* When a condition is met to hide legends in nodes, it works fine and keeps other legends hidden. 
* In the other case, this condition revokes all `show.legend = FALSE` in both nodes and edges. 

Also, I don't understand why the group color does not show in this graph. 

Please share your ideas to improve this code. 
Thank you. 

``` r
library(tidygraph)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'tidygraph'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter
library(ggraph)
#> Loading required package: ggplot2

# Created a tibble graph with highschool in ggraph 
network <- as_tbl_graph(highschool, directed = TRUE) %E>% 
  # add weight to edges 
  mutate(weight = sample(10, n(), replace = TRUE)) %N>% 
  # add group, outdegree to nodes 
  mutate(group = as.factor(sample(3, n(), replace = TRUE)),
         outdegree = centrality_degree(mode = "out", loops = TRUE))

# Made a function to separate graphs by years 
yearly <- function(x) {
  network %E>% 
    filter(year == x) %N>% 
    filter(!node_is_isolated()) 
}

# Made a list contain two graphs 
network_list <- lapply(c(1957:1958), yearly)

set.seed(1000)

# (1) Conditional show.legend in geom_node_point:  
test <- function (y) {
  network_list[[y]] %>% 
    ggraph(layout = "kk") + 
    geom_node_point(aes(color = group), show.legend = ifelse(y == 2, TRUE, FALSE)) + 
    geom_node_point(aes(size = outdegree), show.legend = FALSE) + 
    geom_edge_link(aes(alpha = weight), show.legend = FALSE) + 
    facet_edges(~year)
}
p1 <- test(1) # The node's legend is well hidden, although node's group color is not shown. 
p2 <- test(2) # All node's and edge's legends are shown. 

library(patchwork)
p1 + p2 
```

title: edge_alpha makes ggraph much slower
description:
I built a graph G with 335 vertices and 934 edges (rds is attached as zip).
[G.zip](https://github.com/thomasp85/ggraph/files/3582438/G.zip)
_IGRAPH b2bb788 UNW- 335 934 -- 
attr: name (v/c), n.pubs (v/n), weight (e/n)_

With a code below I observed a dramatic increase in time when activated edge_alpha.
Without edge_alpha the performance time was 1.09 sec, while with edge_alpha time grew up to 26.47 sec!

`G %>% ggraph() + 

geom_edge_link0(edge_width = 0.2, edge_color = "grey50", **edge_alpha = 0.5**) +

geom_point(aes(x=x, y = y), size = 0.5)+ 

theme_graph()+

ggsave("graph.1.png", dpi=400,units="cm", width = 18,height = 10)`

Could you please advise if this is a bug or an inevitable property of ggplot graphics? Is there any way to work around this, I wonder.

title: Incorrect edge attributes depending on loops and end_cap
description:
This seems related to #62, but that issue was closed and I'm seeing this in version 1.0.1.

The below example contains a loop and specifies `end_cap` for the edges, and one of the edges is the wrong color. The next examples show that it plots correctly when the loop is replaced with a non-loop edge, when the loop is listed after the other edges, and when `end_cap` is not specified.

The problem persists when using an undirected graph, when using `geom_edge_link` or `geom_edge_arc` instead of `geom_edge_fan`, and when omitting the `geom_edge_loop` call.

```
library(ggraph)
library(igraph)

## Incorrect when loop listed first
d <- data.frame(node1 = c('C', 'A', 'B'),
                node2 = c('C', 'B', 'A'),
                value = c('Y', 'X', 'X'))
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d, directed = TRUE)
ggraph(g, layout = 'nicely') +
  geom_edge_fan(aes(color = value),
                end_cap = circle(5, 'mm')) +
  geom_edge_loop(aes(color = value)) +
  geom_node_label(aes(label = name))

## Correct when no loop
d <- data.frame(node1 = c('C', 'A', 'B'),
                node2 = c('D', 'B', 'A'),
                value = c('Y', 'X', 'X'))
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d, directed = TRUE)
ggraph(g, layout = 'nicely') +
  geom_edge_fan(aes(color = value),
                end_cap = circle(5, 'mm')) +
  geom_edge_loop(aes(color = value)) +
  geom_node_label(aes(label = name))

## Correct when loop listed third
d <- data.frame(node1 = c('A', 'B', 'C'),
                node2 = c('B', 'A', 'C'),
                value = c('X', 'X', 'Y'))
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d, directed = TRUE)
ggraph(g, layout = 'nicely') +
  geom_edge_fan(aes(color = value),
                end_cap = circle(5, 'mm')) +
  geom_edge_loop(aes(color = value)) +
  geom_node_label(aes(label = name))

## Correct when no end_cap specified
d <- data.frame(node1 = c('C', 'A', 'B'),
                node2 = c('C', 'B', 'A'),
                value = c('Y', 'X', 'X'))
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d, directed = TRUE)
ggraph(g, layout = 'nicely') +
  geom_edge_fan(aes(color = value)) +
  geom_edge_loop(aes(color = value)) +
  geom_node_label(aes(label = name))
```

title: R session crashes due to self-links
description:
First of all, thank you for this great package. I stumbled upon strange behavior: self-links in combination with start_cap/end_cap/arrow definitions occassionally crash the R session. Example:

```
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)

# This works
graph.nocrash <- make_graph(c(1,1,2,2,1,2), directed = T)
ggraph(graph.nocrash, layout = "circle") + 
  geom_node_point() +
  geom_edge_link(start_cap = circle(4,unit="mm"),
                 end_cap = circle(4,unit="mm"),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(4,"mm"))) 

# This crashes R, only difference is the order of edges in make_graph
graph.crash <- make_graph(c(1,1,1,2,2,2), directed = T)

ggraph(graph.crash, layout = "circle") + 
  geom_node_point() +
  geom_edge_link(start_cap = circle(4,unit="mm"),
                 end_cap = circle(4,unit="mm"),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(4,"mm"))) 
```

Sometimes it crashes not at first time, but at second. I guess this depends on the layout.

R version 3.5.3 
ggraph version 1.0.2
igraph version 1.2.4.1

description:
Hi

I had a user report this issue https://github.com/lazappi/clustree/issues/36. After looking into it a bit a think it might be a problem with `ggraph`.

Here is a reprex with an example from one of the vignettes.

``` r
library(ggraph)
#> Loading required package: ggplot2
library(tidygraph)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'tidygraph'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter

set_graph_style(plot_margin = margin(1,1,1,1))
graph <- as_tbl_graph(highschool)

# Not specifying the layout - defaults to "auto"
plot <- ggraph(graph) + 
    geom_edge_link(aes(colour = factor(year))) + 
    geom_node_point()
#> Using `nicely` as default layout
plot
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/eXDu1Ko.png)

That works fine but if we set `options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)` first there is an error when rendering the plot.

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
plot
#> Error in pathAttr(data, length(unique(data$group))): Not compatible with requested type: [type=character; target=integer].

title: Stability Issues?
description:
Hello Thomas,
`ggraph` is wonderful – thank you and your team for putting it together! I have run into a bit of an issue with faceting by a node attribute. Sometimes it will work while others it will not, but I can't figure out where the difference is. There have been times where I have received errors, let everything just sit for a few minutes, and then rerun the same few lines resulting in a successful plot. Because of this, I am unable to provide an example of specific, reproducible code that results in the error. I have repeatedly received the two types of error messages shown below along with how I have tried to fix them. 

Error message 1:
```
Error in gList(list(name = "background.1-19-23-1", gp = NULL, vp = NULL,  : 
  only 'grobs' allowed in "gList"
```
I have no idea how to fix this, but if I remove the `facet_nodes(~node_attribute)` line, everything runs smoothly.

Error message 2:
```
Error in Ops.factor(self$layout$PANEL, i) : 
  level sets of factors are different
```

For this, I have tried changing the attribute, which is numeric, to a factor `facet_nodes(~factor(node_attribute))` but it doesn't fix the problem.

Error message 1 generally arises when my ggraph pipeline gets longer and more complicated. My only intuition about what could be the problem is that my igraph object has a bunch of node attributes (about 20) and I tend to run into this error with my more complex graphs. Still, with these larger objects, it still only breaks sometimes. I have a feeling that if I understood the inner workings of `ggplot2` then I could resolve this, but I was hoping you had some insight.

Thank you and keep up the good work,
Josh Cook

----

### EDIT
I have switched the script to using the `tidygraph` system (instead of a `igraph` + `ggraph`, but the problem persists. I have also tried simplifying the `ggraph` object by `select`ing the node attributes I actually use in the plotting, but that didn't fix the issue, either.

title: dendrogram with branch lengths determined by edge attribute?
description:
this is probably a stupid question,  but it isn't obvious to me how to plot a dendrogram in which branch lengths are determined by the data (i.e. a 'chronogram' in phylogenetics, where branch lengths represent evolutionary time).  Consider this example:

In `ape`, an example phylogeny has branch length data, which is reflected in the plot:

```r
library(ape)
data("bird.orders")
plot(bird.orders)
```

Using the awesome `tidygraph`, we coerce this:

```r
library(tidygraph)
library(ggraph)
bird <- as_tbl_graph(bird.orders) 
```

looks like edge lengths are lost in this transformation? (guess that's a `tidygraph` issue>).  Even if I just manually add a column of branch lengths (below just picking lengths at  random), I'm not sure how to map the `length` column of the edge table to branch lengths to get a plot like the ape plot above...  is this possible with the current layout?  If not, is this something you would consider supporting?  

```r
bird %>% activate(edges) %>%
  mutate(length = abs(rnorm(44))) %>%
  ggraph(layout="dendrogram") + geom_edge_elbow()
```

title: Feature suggestion
description:
Would it be possible to add any of the following suggested options to the ggraph package? (e.g. to the geom_conn_bundle function) To illustrate my suggestions I have made a few dummy plots. These plots represents a small dataset, where node sizes are scaled based on a given measured value for a parameter (values below a given threshold are excluded). Connections are scores of node correlations, where connections not showing significance are removed.

[Examples-of-new-ggplot-options.pdf](https://github.com/thomasp85/ggraph/files/2258778/Examples-of-new-ggplot-options.pdf)

Plot 1 from left:
Added features:	
•	Label-boxes that categorizes related notes, and node-labels of sub-groups within the categories. These are color coded to fit the group-coloring of the nodes.
•	Coloring of connections based on category-subgroups.
•	Scaling of connections based on a score.
•	A label that shows the corresponding values to the connection scale.
Plot 2 from left:
Added features:
•	Label-boxes with sub-group and category-groups reversed from the first plot, and color coded.
•	Connections color-scaled based on a score.
•	A label that shows the corresponding values to the connection-color.
Plot 3 from left:
Added features:
•	Analysis of specific node(s) of interest by emphasizing the connections through coloring connections, while deemphasizing other connections by coloring them a light grey. 
Thank you for your time.
Best Regards,
Stig

title: Feature Request: Automatically set start_cap and end_cap?
description:
Again, thank you for the great tool!  `ggraph` has significantly simplified network visualization within my workflow.

I wonder if there is a reasonable way to automate the use of `start_cap` and `end_cap` (perhaps with a new argument `auto_cap=TRUE` or `start_cap="auto"` and `end_cap="auto"`)?  Specifically, I'm thinking of the following complexities:

* Detect if the nodes are plotted at all (if not, then it would default to no cap offset).
* Detect if only a single node geom is used, and if so, set the caps based on that node type and size.
* Detect if more than one node geom is used, and if so, set the caps based on the size of the largest node size (more precisely, the farthest away from the start and end of the line connecting the nodes or the loop start and end).

Given the need for this to detect aspects about other `geom`s, the solution may benefit from some generalization of the detection of other `geom`s needed in #157.

P.S. Given a suggestion of where to start, I could try for a PR.

title: removing arrowheads in legend
description:
Is there a way to remove arrowheads in the legend? Something like the below would be nice (the guides part)
``` r
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)

set.seed(538)
g <- sample_gnp(n = 30,p = 0.1,directed = T)
E(g)$type <- sample(c(F,T),ecount(g),replace = T)

ggraph(g,layout = "kk")+
  geom_edge_link(aes(col = type),
                 arrow = arrow(type = "closed",length = unit(12,"pt")),
                 end_cap = circle(5,"pt"))+
  geom_node_point(size = 5)+
  theme_graph()+
  guides(edge_colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(arrow = NULL))) 
```
![example](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17147355/61728414-14972100-ad6d-11e9-940e-df678fbba671.png)

What works is overwriting the draw_key function of GeomEdgePath ( [link](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48591582/exclude-arrowheads-in-legend-entry-on-ggplot2) to similar solution for ggplot):
```r
draw_key_line <- function(data, params, size) {
  grid::segmentsGrob(0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5, 
                     gp = grid::gpar(col = alpha(data$edge_colour, data$edge_alpha), 
                               lwd = data$edge_width * .pt, 
                               lty = data$edge_linetype, 
                               lineend = "butt"), arrow = NULL)
}

# override legend drawing function for GeomEdgePath
GeomEdgePath$draw_key <- draw_key_line
```
Don't think that this should be the preferred solution

data.frame(from = c("a", "b"),

title: Preserving string-ness
description:
I don't know if this is an error or not, but is there a way to prevent character vectors in mappings to be turned into factors?

In the code below, I create a small graph and I provide a string vector for `edge.id` (and another, `other_string`, in case `edge.id` is treated specially (which doesn't seem to be the case)). I want to be able to map edge ids to other labels in a table, so I would like the vector(s) to be strings that I can access inside the aesthetics. I don't use a table in the example but a function so I can print the parameter, and that shows that these string vectors have been turned into factors. 

```r
library(tibble)
library(tidygraph)
library(ggraph)
nodes <- tribble(
    ~label,
    "foo",
    "bar",
    "baz",
)
edges <- tribble(
    ~from, ~to, ~edge.id, ~other_string,
    "foo", "bar", "foobar", "qux",
    "foo", "baz", "foobaz", "qax"
)
tg <- tbl_graph(nodes = nodes, edges = edges)
tg

map_id <- function(ids) {
    print(ids)
    as.character(ids)
}
ggraph::ggraph(tg) +
    ggraph::geom_edge_link(
        aes(label = map_id(edge.id))
    )
ggraph::ggraph(tg) +
    ggraph::geom_edge_link(
        aes(label = map_id(other_string))
    )
```

I can, of course, turn them back into strings, but that seems like a roundabout way to do this.

title: error messages for incorrect `aes()` specification?
description:
In light of this issue on [SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50195199/geom-edge-link-in-ggraph-wont-let-me-specify-edge-colour), it might be helpful if the `geom_*_*` arguments to `aes()` spit out a warning or error message if the user supplies a string that is not an attribute of the network?

E.g.,

```
ggraph(ring) +
geom_edge_link(aes(edge_colour='grey'))
```

if `'grey'` is not an edge attribute, a warning is produced like `"Grey" is not an edge attribute of graph "ring". Are you sure you don't want geom_edge_link(colour='grey')"`.

This is in line with the type of errors that other tidyverse packages are producing.

title: Geometries in aes() fail with no data
description:
This is a somewhat esoteric issue. I'm working on a package using (the really fantastic) `ggraph` where different groups are getting different edge geoms. However, as it's happening programmatically in certain functions, I don't always know if all groups have data corresponding to them. Functions that call, e.g. `label_rect()` or any of the functions that are of class `geometry ` in `aes()`, fail when there is no corresponding data. This seems to be related to using those geometry functions in `aes()` specifically.

Here's an example using the friend/foe graph from the edge vignette. Where all groups are present, it runs fine: 

```r 
library(ggraph)
library(tidygraph)
library(igraph)
library(dplyr)

simple <- make_graph('bull')
V(simple)$name <- c('Thomas', 'Bob', 'Hadley', 'Winston', 'Baptiste')
E(simple)$type <- sample(c('friend', 'foe'), 5, TRUE)

# filter out foes
friend_edge_data <- function(layout) {
  get_short_edges <- get_edges()
  layout %>% 
    create_layout("graphopt") %>% 
    get_short_edges() %>% 
    filter(type == "friend")
}

# filter out friends
foe_edge_data <- function(layout) {
  get_short_edges <- get_edges()
  layout %>% 
    create_layout("graphopt") %>% 
    get_short_edges() %>% 
    filter(type == "foe")
}

# this works fine because there is data for both friends and foes
ggraph(simple, layout = 'graphopt') + 
  geom_edge_link(data = friend_edge_data, aes(start_cap = label_rect(node1.name),
                     end_cap = label_rect(node2.name)), 
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(4, 'mm'))) + 
  geom_edge_arc(data = foe_edge_data, aes(start_cap = label_rect(node1.name),
                     end_cap = label_rect(node2.name)), 
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(4, 'mm'))) + 
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name))
```

But if a group is missing data, it fails.

```r 
# peace reigns and everyone is friends now
E(simple)$type <- sample(c('friend'), 10, TRUE)

#this fails because there are no foes
ggraph(simple, layout = 'graphopt') + 
  geom_edge_link(data = friend_edge_data, aes(start_cap = label_rect(node1.name),
                                              end_cap = label_rect(node2.name)), 
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(4, 'mm'))) + 
  geom_edge_arc(data = foe_edge_data, aes(start_cap = label_rect(node1.name),
                                          end_cap = label_rect(node2.name)), 
                arrow = arrow(length = unit(4, 'mm'))) + 
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name))
```

In my code, I worked around this issue by marking the data NULL in some of the Stat methods, e.g.:

```r 
StatEdgeLink <- ggplot2::ggproto('StatEdgeLink', ggraph::StatEdgeLink,
                                setup_data = function(data, params) {
                                 #  ... some setup related to my specific needs
                                  if (nrow(data) > 0) {
                                    data <- ggraph::StatEdgeLink$setup_data(data, params)
                                  } else {
                                    data <- NULL
                                  }
                                  data
                                },
                                compute_panel = function(data, scales, n = 100) {
                                  if (is.null(data)) return(data)
                                  ggraph::StatEdgeLink$compute_panel(data, scales, n = n)
                                })

StatEdgeArc <- ggplot2::ggproto('StatEdgeArc', ggraph::StatEdgeArc,
                                 setup_data = function(data, params) {
                                  #  ... some setup related to my specific needs
                                   if (nrow(data) > 0) {
                                     data <- ggraph::StatEdgeArc$setup_data(data, params)
                                   } else {
                                      data <- NULL
                                    }
                                   data
                                 })
```

But I'm not sure if that's a good solution to suggest (in particular because the main issue seems to be putting non-data, the geometry functions, into the `aes()` call; `ggplot2` otherwise handles a set of `aes()` + missing data quite genially), or if the issue even bothers you that much. 

Thanks!
Malcolm

Plotting empty graph or graph without edges
description:
While using `ggraph` (current version on CRAN, R 3.3.1) for plotting my `igraph` graphs, I found that the plotting of empty graphs or graphs without edges results in an error (see below for an example). 

In my scripts, I heavily use `igraph::induced_subgraph` and it may happen that the induced subgraphs do not have edges. While checking for the error, I noticed that it also occurs if the given graph is completely empty (no vertices).

Is it possible to change `ggraph` to get an empty plotting pane when giving an empty graph or just plotting the nodes when there are no edges connecting them? 
Let me know if I can help somehow. And thank you for your nice work on this package.

### Example


```R
requireNamespace("igraph")
requireNamespace("gglot2")
requireNamespace("ggraph")

# g <- igraph::sample_pa(10, directed = TRUE) # works fine
# g <- igraph::make_empty_graph(n = 0, directed = FALSE) # no vertices, does not work
g <- igraph::make_empty_graph(n = 2, directed = FALSE) # no edges, does not work

VERTEX.SIZE <- 7
p <- ggraph::ggraph(g, layout = "nicely") +
    ggraph::geom_node_point(color = "red", size = VERTEX.SIZE) +
    ggraph::geom_edge_fan(
        end_cap = ggraph::circle(VERTEX.SIZE + 3, 'pt'),
        start_cap = ggraph::circle(VERTEX.SIZE + 3, 'pt'),
        arrow = if (igraph::is.directed(g)) {
            ggplot2::arrow(length = ggplot2::unit(VERTEX.SIZE / 2, 'pt'), ends = "last", type = "closed")
        } else {
            NULL
        }
    )
print(p)
```

The error I get is the following:
> \> p <- ggraph::ggraph(g, layout = "nicely") +
> \+     ggraph::geom_node_point(color = "red", size = VERTEX.SIZE) +
> \+     ggraph::geom_edge_link(
> \+         end_cap = ggraph::circle(VERTEX.SIZE + 3, 'pt'),
> \+         start_cap = ggraph::circle(VERTEX.SIZE + 3, 'pt')
> \+     )
> \> print(p)
> Error in `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, "circular", value = FALSE) :

When I use the completely empty graph, I get the following error:

> \+     ggraph::geom_edge_link(

>   replacement has 1 row, data has 0
> \> print(p)
> Error in print(p) : object 'p' not found

### Side note on `igraph` behavior

I tried `igraph` to plot the graphs and it is able to plot an edgeless graph (try `igraph::plot.igraph(igraph::make_empty_graph(n = 2))`), although it also fails for the empty graph (`igraph::plot.igraph(igraph::make_empty_graph(n = 0))`).

```
ggraph(gg, layout = 'linear', circular=T) + 
	geom_edge_fan(aes(width=weight, label=round(weight,2)), 
		                   end_cap = circle(.5, 'cm'),
			           angle_calc='along', label_dodge=unit(-0.3, "cm")) + 	
	geom_edge_loop(aes(width=weight, direction=rep(c(30,270,150),3), label=round(weight,2)),
				    end_cap = circle(.5, 'cm'),
				    angle_calc='along', label_dodge=unit(-0.3, "cm")) +
		geom_node_point(size=12)

```
The edge widths are correct again if we remove the `end_cap` spec:
```
ggraph(gg, layout = 'linear', circular=T) + 
	geom_edge_fan(aes(width=weight, label=round(weight,2)), 
		                 #end_cap = circle(.5, 'cm'),
				   angle_calc='along', label_dodge=unit(-0.3, "cm")) + 	
	geom_edge_loop(aes(width=weight, direction=rep(c(30,270,150),3), label=round(weight,2)),
				 #end_cap = circle(.5, 'cm'),
				   angle_calc='along', label_dodge=unit(-0.3, "cm")) +
	geom_node_point(size=12)

```

title: Plot networks from lavaan?
description:
It would be neat if this package could implement the functionality that semPlot has.

http://sachaepskamp.com/semPlot/examples#Lavaan

It can extract the edge list/connection matrix from **lavaan** or **lm** class objects and automatically plot them. The results are not very pretty and hard to deal with because it's based on base plot. So I'm looking for some **ggplot2** based solution for plotting SEMs. Right now I manually draw SEMs using e.g. [draw.io](http://draw.io) or Google Draw. This is quite time-consuming, especially when updating numbers  on paths.

I managed to convert that into an **igraph** object and plot it.

```
library(pacman)
p_load(lavaan, magrittr, igraph)

#fit simple reg
fit = sem("Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width + Petal.Length", data = iris)
fit_params = fit %>% parameterestimates()
fit_betas = fit_params %>% dplyr::filter(op == "~") %>% `[`("est") %>% unlist

#adj mats
beta_mat = fit@Model@GLIST$beta
log_mat = (fit@Model@GLIST$beta != 0)
adj_mat = log_mat %>% as.integer %>% matrix(nrow = nrow(fit@Model@GLIST$beta), byrow = T)
rownames(adj_mat) = colnames(adj_mat) = fit@Data@ov.names[[1]]
betas = beta_mat[log_mat]

#to igraph
adj_mat %>% 
  graph_from_adjacency_matrix() %>% 
  plot.igraph(edge.label = betas %>% round(2)
              )

#alternative approach
fit_params %>% 
  dplyr::filter(op == "~") %>% 
  `[`(c("rhs", "lhs")) %>% 
  as.matrix %>% 
  graph_from_edgelist %>% 
  plot.igraph(edge.label = fit_betas %>% round(2))

```

I was not able to get further because of #34.

title: infinite arrows if ..index.. is used in edge aesthetic
description:
If you use ..index.. in your edge aesthetic you don't get just one arrow at the end of your edge, but a lot of arrows at every point of the edge.

Here is a reproducible example 
`play_islands(5, 4, 1, 2) %>% 
  ggraph() +
  geom_node_point() +
  geom_edge_link(aes(alpha = 0.4),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(4, 'mm')), 
                 start_cap = circle(3, 'mm'),
                 end_cap = circle(3, 'mm'),

But the graph should look more like this:

title: Combine ggraph with ggmap
description:

Here's the code I'm running to create the graph and the map:

```
# Create graph

    mutate(line = as.factor(line)) %>% 
    graph_from_data_frame(directed = FALSE, vertices = stations)

# Create graph layout

# Set up colours

    geom_node_point(size = .5) +
    geom_edge_fan(aes(colour = line_name, edge_width = daily_trips), 
                  show.legend = F, edge_alpha = 1) +
    scale_edge_colour_manual(name = "Line", values = line_cols) +
    theme_void() 


map <- get_map(location = c(lon = -0.1275, lat = 51.5072), maptype = "toner-lite")
map_plot <- ggmap(map)

title: ggraph doesn't respect color palettes for edges?
description:
Possibly I'm just missing something obvious here.

Using the default hairball from the [Edges Vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ggraph/vignettes/Edges.html) here:

```r
ggraph(hairball, layout = 'kk') + 
  geom_node_point(aes(colour = pop_devel), size=3) +
  geom_edge_link(aes(colour = year)) + 
  ggthemes::scale_colour_ptol() 
```

I'm getting the pallette colors working for the nodes, but having no change on the edge colors: 

![ex](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/222586/39770696-9ac73424-52a4-11e8-9796-21b4f563c57c.png)

What did I miss?  It would be great to be able to leverage the usual awesome `ggplot` palette stuff here. Thanks!

title: Plot limits don't update when using large size of nodes
description:
The limits of the plot produced by `ggraph` don't seem to update when using the `size` aesthetics of the nodes (and so the larger nodes appear "cut" by the border of the plot):

```
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)

m <- structure(c(0, 0.58, 0, 0.34, 0, NA, 0, 0, 0.12, 0, NA, NA, 0, 
0, 0.27, NA, NA, NA, 0, 0, NA, NA, NA, NA, 0), .Dim = c(5L, 5L
), .Dimnames = list(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"), c("A", "B", "C", 
"D", "E")))

diag(m) <- 0
ex_g <- graph.adjacency(m, mode = "lower", weighted = TRUE)
V(ex_g)$size <- c(4, 3.5, 3, 3, 2)
E(ex_g)$weight[is.na(E(ex_g)$weight)] <- 0

p_ex_graph <- ggraph(ex_g, layout = "igraph", algorithm = "fr", niter = 5000)

p_ex_graph + 
  geom_edge_link(aes(edge_width = weight), colour = "grey50", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_node_point(aes(size = size), fill = "grey70", colour = "grey10", show.legend = FALSE, shape = 21) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name)) +
  scale_size(range = c(6, 20)) +
  scale_edge_width_continuous(range = c(1, 3)) +
  theme_graph()
```
![rplot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/515259/39278423-20bb1ef4-4947-11e8-94ef-a51017bb59e8.png)

I've reproduced the problem on both the CRAN and the latest dev version.

title: Turn off lines in dendrogram legends?
description:
Thanks for this brilliant package. I really love to be able to use the grammar of graphics with network plots. It makes the whole thing a lot more versatile!

I just can't figure out one detail:

### Problem
When plotting dendrograms and setting `show.legend = TRUE` in both the edges and nodes, the legend shows lines with points in it for both types. This makes total sense in networks but it makes it hard to distinguish colours in this case and shapes in other dendrograms I've plotted:
```
# Make dendrogram
hc <- hclust(dist(mtcars))
hierarchy <- stats::as.dendrogram(hc)
# Add colours
hierarchy <- stats::dendrapply(hierarchy, function(x) {
  if (stats::is.leaf(x)) {
    attr(x, "Colour") <- ifelse(attr(x, "label") == "Hornet 4 Drive",
                                 "a", 
                                 "c")
  } else {
    attr(x, "Colour") <- "b"
  }
  attr(x, "edgePar") <- list(cols = attr(x, "Colour"))
  attr(x, "nodePar") <- list(cols = attr(x, "Colour"))
  x
})

# Use ggraph for beautiful dendrogram
library("ggraph")
ggraph(hierarchy,layout = "dendrogram",
       circular = FALSE) +
  geom_edge_elbow(aes(colour = cols,
                      edge_linetype = cols),
                  show.legend = TRUE) +
  geom_node_point(aes(filter = leaf,
                      colour = cols,
                      shape = cols),
                  show.legend = TRUE,
                  size = 3) +
  theme_graph()
```
![rplot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23524101/39042344-7611d2d6-4482-11e8-8d45-5c8a14f33040.png)

### Expected Behaviour/Request/Question
It would be nice if it was possible to turn off the 'merging' of the legends. Either in an option or via the `guides` command.

### What I've tried
Some people on SO suggest to manipulate the legend directly with specifications to `guides`:
```
guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = 0)),
       colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = 0)),
       line = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = 0)),
       edge_linetype = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = 0)),
       point = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = 0)))
``` 
Note, that I just tried every guide I could think of because I'm not sure which one controls the legends I have. But nothing happens anyway.

title: Some scale_edge_* only work when ggraph is loaded
description:
It appears some scales only work when ggraph is actually loaded. When referring to them with `::` the correct guide cannot be found. When the guide is manually specified, the scale does work (with a warning), but no guide is shown.

```
data('highschool', package = 'ggraph')
graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(highschool)

ggraph::ggraph(graph, layout = 'kk') + 
  ggraph::geom_edge_link(ggplot2::aes(color = year)) + 
  ggraph::scale_edge_color_gradient()
# Error in get(as.character(FUN), mode = "function", envir = envir) : 
#   object 'guide_edge_colourbar' of mode 'function' was not found

ggraph::ggraph(graph, layout = 'kk') + 
  ggraph::geom_edge_link(ggplot2::aes(color = year)) + 
  ggraph::scale_edge_color_gradient(guide = ggraph::guide_edge_colorbar())
# Warning message:
#   In guide_train.colorbar(guide, scale) :
#   colorbar guide needs colour or fill scales.
```

These examples do work after `library(ggraph)`.

I believe this will be a problem for code in packages, as `requireNamespace` does not appear to alleviate the problem.

title: Consider an adjacency matrix plotting format?
description:
First, thanks for sharing this awesome package, and I greatly appreciate the detailed vignettes.  Just a quick suggestion here.  

Sometimes it is easier to visualize connections as an adjacency matrix rather than as a line/arc between two points.  Consider examples shown here: https://matthewlincoln.net/2014/12/20/adjacency-matrix-plots-with-r-and-ggplot2.html, or commonly used in ecological networks where it can be much easier to see bipartite and nested structures, e.g. compare:

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cboettig/EcoNetGen/v0.1.0-1/man/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-2-1.png)

to the same network with typical edge based plot:

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cboettig/EcoNetGen/v0.1.0-1/man/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-3-1.png)

Both show four "modules" but the adjacency matrix makes it clear that modules have a distinct (bipartite nested) structure.  Simple enough to do with `geom_raster` but would still be nice as part of network visualization in `ggraph`.

title: Error in geom_node_point aesthetics. Object not found.
description:
I am encountering an error when trying to pass aesthetics to `geom_node_point` while passing the same aesthetic to `geom_edge_link` works flawlessly.

This produces the expected result:
```
library(tidygraph)
library(ggraph)
edges <- data.frame(from = "source",
                    to = 1:20,
                    total = sample(1:9,20, replace = TRUE),
                    color = as.factor(rep(c("red","blue"),10)))
n_list <- data.frame(nodes = c(1:20, "source"))
example_graph <- tbl_graph(edges = edges, nodes = n_list)
ggraph(example_graph, layout = "kk") +
geom_node_point() + geom_edge_link(aes(alpha = total, color = color)) + theme_graph()
```

ggraph(example_graph, layout = "kk") +

title: bad interface to viridis api
description:
Hello,

I have run into an issue using viridis with ggraph. The call stack is
```
[[1]]
scale_edge_color_viridis(discrete = FALSE, option = "plasma")

[[2]]
scale_edge_colour_gradientn(colours = viridis(256, alpha, begin, 
    end, option), ...)

[[3]]
viridis(256, alpha, begin, end, option)
```
. Option is a character vector and signature of viridis is

```
function (n, alpha = 1, begin = 0, end = 1, direction = 1, option = "D") 
```

so option value is passed to direction and it blows up on a mathematical calculation.

Looks like a quick fix.

Thanks,

Slava

title: ViridisLite update causing downstream issues
description:
I received the following error when trying to load ggraph:
```
Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘viridis’:
 object ‘cividis’ is not exported by 'namespace:viridisLite'
```
I think this is because viridis 0.5 depends on viridisLite 0.3.0, but ggraph only installs viridisLite 0.2.0.
See here: https://github.com/sjmgarnier/viridis/issues/52

It turns out that the issue can be solved by manually installing viridisLite, but I'm guessing there's a way to make this happen automagically in ggplot?

title: Move roxygen to markdown format
Clipping issue
description: I don't know if this is a problem with gridExtra::grid.arrange or ggraph, but there is an issue with parts of graphs being clipped. Consider the code: ```r devtools::install_github("mailund/ralgo") library(ralgo) plots <- vector("list", 4) tree <- empty_search_tree() for (i in 1:4) { tree <- insert(tree, i) plots[[i]] <- plot(tree) } ``` Here I construct four search tree plots and save them in a list. If I print one of them I get a plot where all of the graph is visible. ```r plots[[3]] ``` If I want to add all four plots in a grid, however, the top of the graphs get clipped ```r gridExtra::grid.arrange(plots[[1]], plots[[2]], plots[[3]], plots[[4]], nrow = 2) ``` (the red oval annotations are for highlighting the problem; they are not part of the plot). I suspect it is an issue with the size of the nodes. I use size 10 for the inner nodes and the clipping issue goes away if I use half the size, but I would expect that a bounding box for a plot would take node size into account?

title: geom_edge_link doesn't handle graphs without edges.
description: For the special case where a graph doesn't have any edges, calling `geom_edge_link`. For example, with a simple graph with three nodes and no edges, you can plot it if you do not call `geom_edge_link()`: ```r graph <- list(nodes = tibble(1:3), edges = tibble(from = vector("numeric"), to = vector("numeric"))) tbl_graph(graph$nodes, graph$edges) %>% ggraph(layout = "tree") + geom_node_point() + theme_graph() ``` The result isn't that exciting, it is just three dots, but here it is: If you then also call `geom_edge_link`, you get an error: ```r tbl_graph(graph$nodes, graph$edges) %>% ggraph(layout = "tree") + geom_node_point() + geom_edge_link() + theme_graph() ``` ``` Error in `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, "circular", value = FALSE) : replacement has 1 row, data has 0 ``` I would expect it to just not draw any edges.

title: Dendrogram layout fails with error "object 'direction' not found"
description:
This is a more general version of the errors reported in #72 and #79.

The code (verbatim from several examples)

```r
fgraph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(flare$edges, vertices = flare$vertices)
ggraph(fgraph, layout = "dendrogram") +
  geom_edge_elbow()
```

fails with (as in #72):

    Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'direction' not found

Passing e.g. `direction = "out"` in either `ggraph()` or in `geom_edge_elbow` itself yields the same error. Wrapping it in an `aes()` call, e.g.

```r
ggraph(fgraph, layout = "dendrogram") +
  geom_edge_elbow(aes(direction = "out"))
```

emits the warning (as in #79)

    Warning message:
    Removed 251 rows containing non-finite values (stat_edge_elbow).

and draws an empty plot.

title: Modifying the dataframe in between creating the layout and plotting
description:
A minimal example of what I'd like to do is plot a tree, and then draw a rectangle under each branch of a tree to highlight some particular structure.

Here's some code attempting that:
```
iris[,1:4] %>% 
  dist() %>% 
  hclust() %>% 
  as.dendrogram() %>% 
  create_layout(., layout = "dendrogram") %>% 
  ggraph() + geom_edge_link() + 
  geom_node_text(aes(label = ggraph.index)) +
  geom_node_tile(aes(width = 20, 
                     height = y, 
                     y = y/2, 
                     fill = factor(ggraph.index), 
                     filter = ggraph.index %in% c(143,298)),
                 alpha= 0.5, colour = NA)
```

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/13338560/25406531/014fc6b0-29d5-11e7-953c-815d303d6fe0.png)


I hard-coded in the `ggraph.index` value because I couldn't see any other way to identify those nodes, but that's not an insurmountable problem. Really the issue is that I'd like to do something like:

```
iris[,1:4] %>% 
  dist() %>% 
  hclust() %>% 
  as.dendrogram() %>% 
  create_layout(., layout = "dendrogram") %>% 
  mutate(fac = cut(ggraph.index, c(0,143,298))) %>%    # define groups
  group_by(fac) %>%                                    # group by clusters
  mutate(groupxmin = min(x), groupxmax = max(x)) %>%   # find extents of all leaves within each group
  ggraph() + 
  geom_edge_link() + 
  geom_node_tile(aes(width = groupxmax-groupxmin,      # plot width to correct extents
                     height = y,
                     x = (groupxmax+groupxmin)/2,      # center on the extents
                     y = y/2,
                     fill = fac,
                     filter = ggraph.index %in% c(143,298)),
                 alpha= 0.5, colour = NA)

```

The first part of this code (prior to the `ggraph()` call) generates exactly the dataframe I'd like:

```

title: Question: Best recommendation for using ggraph to plot a DAG?
description:
I have only been experimenting with this package for a weekend, and already I am finding it a highly compelling alternative to other graph visualization packages for R. Thank you for your work.

In the domain which I work, I frequently report results utilizing plots of networks which are DAG's. The best way that I have found to do this in R (before discovering `ggraph` I think) is using the `DOT` layout from `graph viz` provided within [DiagrammeR](http://rich-iannone.github.io/DiagrammeR/graphviz_and_mermaid.html)

What your recommendations for best plotting DAG's using `ggraph`? I have tried the `dendrogram` layout, but it appears to force a strict definition of a dendrogram (which it should) and does not let me control the direction of the layout (for example, left to right). Are some of the `graph viz` layouts available in `ggraph`?

Thank you for your work. I am looking forward to utilizing this package frequently.

title: allow using ggraph *without* attaching it
description:
```
library(ggraph)
library(igraph)
graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(highschool)

# Not specifying the layout - defaults to "auto"
g <- ggraph(graph) + 
  geom_edge_link(aes(colour = factor(year))) + 
  geom_node_point()
g
```
This is fine:

![rplot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5372770/30227310-82bddee8-94d9-11e7-85e6-d86f8977efc9.png)

However, when plotted without `ggraph` attached, the legend is missing and there are different colors.

```
detach(name = "package:ggraph", unload = TRUE)
g  # without legend
```

![rplot01](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5372770/30227696-d8070482-94da-11e7-8393-24bbbb1ec844.png)

I am (wildly) guessing this has something to do with the black magic of the edge aesthetics that `ggraph` does.

This is not a problem in a script use (where usually you'd have `library(ggraph)`), but it can be a little odd in in-package use:
I'd rather not import the entire `ggraph` namespace, but *without* that, my examples on `ggraph`-derivative functions will not work properly (as in the above).

The behavior also strikes me as a little unexpected because, `class(g)` is only `"gg"     "ggplot"`, which makes me think that *just* `ggplot::print.ggplot()` ought to do the trick.

Is there any chance this could be changed?

title: Sankey layout
Can't set fixed color for edges with color =
description:
Setting a color outside the `aes` doesn't work with `color = ` or `colour =`. Reproducible example:

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)

data_frame("a", "b") %>%
  graph_from_data_frame() %>%
  ggraph(layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(color = "green")
#> Error: Unknown parameters: colour
```

This does work if I set it to `edge_colour` (not `colour`, or `edge_color`, which give similar errors). This makes some sense to me in that the fixed aesthetic names aren't expanded.

Note that the docs for the function say it's possible to set a fixed color with the `color =` argument:

> other arguments passed on to layer. There are three types of arguments you can use here:
>     * Aesthetics: to set an aesthetic to a fixed value, like color = "red" or size = 3.

title: "promise already under evaluation" with geom_node_text(..., repel = TRUE)
description:
Hi,

I've hit a problem when calling `geom_node_text()` with the `repel = TRUE` parameter.  See https://github.com/dgrtwo/tidy-text-mining/issues/27 for more detail, but in summary:

```
data_frame(node1 = 1:4, node2 = 2:5) %>%
    graph_from_data_frame() %>%
    ggraph(layout = "fr") +
    geom_edge_link() +
    geom_node_point() +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE)
```

throws

> Error in data.frame(x = xlim, y = ylim) : 
>   promise already under evaluation: recursive default argument reference or earlier problems?
> 

By comparison, replacing `repel = TRUE` with `vjust = 1, hjust = 1`:

```
data_frame(node1 = 1:4, node2 = 2:5) %>%
    graph_from_data_frame() %>%
    ggraph(layout = "fr") +
    geom_edge_link() +
    geom_node_point() +
    geom_node_text(aes(label = name), vjust = 1, hjust = 1)
```

 (as suggested in the above link) runs fine.

Apologies if the source of the error is a different package; happy to raise it elsewhere if need be.

title: Fix position
description:
Looking forward to the development of this package!.   This is more of a feature request than an issue. I was just wondering if it is or will be possible to fix the position of a network layout.  i.e. if you were to re-execute this code: 

`ggraph(graph = gr, layout = 'fr') + 
  geom_edge_link(aes(size = weight), color = 'grey', alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_node_point(aes(color = class), size = 10) + 
  coord_fixed() + 
  ggforce::theme_no_axes()`

that the layout would always be the same?  I don't think this is doable through igraph and perhaps that means also not possible here?  My rationale is because it would be great to be able to update the same network temporally showing how edges change - this would only make sense visually if the nodes remain in the same place.
